## Rationale

- **TOOL-306 CORE API** (Adopt): The single best surprise of the discovery sweep: works keyless from this container with real, large result sets, contradicting a plausible assumption that CORE needs a key. Directly answers the needs-table's 'which free keyed services would unblock discovery' question by showing CORE needs none. Also doubles as a full-text-access path (aggregates repository copies). Serves W1/W2 discovery and sub-task 3 (full-text access). Evidence: python3 research/tools/polite_get.py 'https://api.core.ac.uk/v3/search/works?q=pdf+repair&limit=1' -> HTTP 200, totalHits=4978068, 2026-09-27 (probe/core.json); CORE's own terms page confirms keyless access at 'one batch request or five single requests per 10 seconds' with no registration required
- **TOOL-300 Crossref REST API** (Adopt): Already the KB's main discovery+metadata backbone (used throughout research/sources/registry.jsonl). OBS-0600 shows it is the more complete of the two free forward-citation sources (0/10 zero-count sources vs OpenCitations' 5/10). Also answers sub-task 7: DOI to BibTeX/CSL via /works/<doi>/transform/<mime> works keyless, tested live. Serves W1/W2 discovery and P4 full review broadly; feeds forward-citation checks for any gap that depends on knowing whether a source has since been superseded or corroborated. Evidence: python3 research/tools/polite_get.py 'https://api.crossref.org/works?query.bibliographic=pdf+repair&rows=1' -> HTTP 200, total-results=457305; works/<doi>, journals/<issn>/works and content-negotiation to application/x-bibtex all returned HTTP 200 on 2026-09-27 (see OBS-0600 and probe/crossref*.json, probe/das2018.bib)
- **TOOL-310 Unpaywall API** (Adopt): Confirms the needs-table's 'Unpaywall works keyless' state with a fresh, dated, first-hand test (previously only asserted, not independently re-verified this session). Correctly reports closed access for a known-closed IEEE paper, giving confidence in its accuracy. Directly serves sub-task 3 (full-text access) alongside CORE and direct PDF fetch. Evidence: python3 research/tools/polite_get.py 'https://api.unpaywall.org/v2/10.1109/das.2018.64?email=research@pdfpundit.invalid' -> HTTP 200, {"is_oa":false,"oa_status":"closed",...}, 2026-09-27 (probe/unpaywall.json)
- **TOOL-323 PyMuPDF4LLM (pymupdf4llm)** (Adopt): The strongest hands-on result of this sweep: real heading structure plus a cleaner two-column read than either pdfplumber or the existing pdftotext baseline, directly useful for isolating a paper's Conclusion/Limitations text for sub-task 5. Its AGPL-3.0-or-later licence (the free option of the dual licence) is copyleft: fine for this research pipeline's own internal use (we are not distributing it or linking it into the PDFPundit product, which is the pure-Rust/lopdf-only artifact under the charter's clean-room rule), but flag it clearly so no one later vendors its output-generation code into the shipped tool. Evidence: OBS-0601: pip-installed into a scratch venv (369 MB total with pdfplumber, deleted after) and run on the cached CPR PDF: converted to Markdown in 7.9s, correctly leveled every section heading (Introduction..Conclusion), located '### References' as its own heading with individually separated entries, and stayed column-clean at the same two-column boundary where pdfplumber and pdftotext both garbled the text; 2026-09-27
- **TOOL-304 OpenAlex API** (Trial): Confirms the needs-table's 'OpenAlex returns 429 without keys' state with a fresh test. OpenAlex's polite-pool/mailto and free-API-key mechanism is well documented (docs.openalex.org/how-to-use-the-api, which now redirects to help.openalex.org) but this agent could not pull today's exact numeric quota through WebFetch's page summarizer on 2026-09-27, so the specific rate-limit figures below are not independently reconfirmed this session and should be treated as Assess-level until a future agent re-checks them directly. Recommended for the API-account list (see report.md): likely the single highest-value free key for W1, since OpenAlex indexes IEEE/ACM/Elsevier venues that OpenCitations under-covers (OBS-0600). Evidence: python3 research/tools/polite_get.py 'https://api.openalex.org/works?search=pdf+repair&per-page=1' -> HTTP 429 twice (60s backoff each), 2026-09-27; not retried further
- **TOOL-301 OpenCitations (Index API v2 / COCI)** (Trial): OBS-0600: agrees closely with Crossref for ACM/Elsevier/PoPETs venues, but under-covers IEEE and 2024+ works (misses 2 citations Crossref already has for SRC-0112, a 2024 IEEE TIFS paper), confirming the needs-table's DAS-2018/CPR observation and extending it. Use as a secondary cross-check, not the primary source: Crossref (TOOL-300) is more complete. Serves W1/W2 forward-citation coverage; backs OBS-0600. Evidence: python3 research/tools/polite_get.py 'https://opencitations.net/index/api/v2/citations/doi:10.1109/das.2018.64' -> HTTP 200, body [] (0 citers), 2026-09-27; run again for 10 sources in OBS-0600
- **TOOL-305 Semantic Scholar Graph API** (Trial): Confirms the needs-table's 'Semantic Scholar returns 429 without keys' state with a fresh test. semanticscholar.org/product/api documents a free API-key request form ('you will receive your private API key via email'); this agent could not extract today's exact numeric rate-limit figures via WebFetch's summarizer (one fetch attempt returned an implausible '1000 requests per second' figure that looks like a misread and is not trusted), so treat any specific quota number as unverified until a future agent confirms it directly against the live docs. Recommended for the API-account list alongside OpenAlex. Evidence: python3 research/tools/polite_get.py 'https://api.semanticscholar.org/graph/v1/paper/search?query=pdf+repair&limit=1' -> HTTP 429 twice (60s backoff each), 2026-09-27; not retried further
- **TOOL-302 arXiv API (export.arxiv.org)** (Trial): Contradicts the needs-table's 'arXiv id lookups work' note as tested today; most likely transient shared-IP contention from other Stage-2 agents hitting export.arxiv.org concurrently (MIN_GAP=3s is per-process, not per-container-wide across agents), not a permanent block. Still needed for GROBID/Nougat benchmark papers (arXiv 2303.09957, 2410.09871) which the chair should re-fetch via WebFetch/browser if the API stays flaky. Re-test before relying on it in P4. Evidence: python3 research/tools/polite_get.py 'https://export.arxiv.org/api/query?id_list=2101.00001' -> HTTP 406 twice (60s backoff each), 2026-09-27, despite this being a documented known-good id lookup; not retried further per the no-retry-loop rule
- **TOOL-317 GROBID (CRF-only Docker image)** (Trial): At ~486 MiB the CRF-only image comfortably fits the 1.5 GB/tool budget (full image is ~14 GB, out of the question). arXiv 2303.09957 (found via SRCH-0617) reports GROBID best-in-class for academic-PDF metadata/reference extraction among 10 compared tools, which is strong published support for making it the primary reference-list extractor once a future agent (with Docker access) can actually run it. Recommend a P4 hands-on trial the moment a Docker daemon is available. Evidence: Image size confirmed via Docker Hub v2 API: GET https://hub.docker.com/v2/repositories/grobid/grobid/tags -> grobid/grobid:0.9.1-crf full_size=509986678 bytes (~486 MiB), 2026-09-27 (probe/dockerhub_grobid.json). Hands-on run not attempted: starting the Docker daemon (`nohup dockerd &`) was denied by the sandbox's auto-mode classifier ('[Unauthorized Persistence]'); per the coordinator's mid-task update this was not retried or worked around.
- **TOOL-320 MinerU** (Trial): The brief's '2509 is AGPL' warning is confirmed exactly: MinerU v2.5.0 (tagged Sept 2025) is AGPL-3.0, a copyleft licence PDFPundit's clean-room rule would flag for any linked/derivative use; but the current v4.0.7 (and PyPI 'mineru') has since relicensed to Apache-2.0 plus a commercial-MAU/revenue-threshold addendum, which is compatible with research use and most non-trivial commercial use. Any future agent must pin the exact version used and re-check LICENSE.md at that tag, since this project has changed licence at least once. Evidence: License history resolved by direct fetch, not memory: raw.githubusercontent.com/opendatalab/MinerU/master/LICENSE.md (current) begins 'MinerU is licensed under Apache License 2.0 and is subject to the additional terms below... Commercial License and Thresholds', fetched 2026-09-27 (probe/mineru_license.md); the git tag mineru-2.5.0-released (matching the brief's '2509' = Sept 2025) instead has raw.githubusercontent.com/opendatalab/MinerU/mineru-2.5.0-released/LICENSE.md as the full GNU AGPLv3 text, fetched 2026-09-27 (probe/mineru_2.5.0_license.md). PyPI metadata's own license field is null for the current release.
- **TOOL-322 pdfplumber** (Trial): Runs cleanly and is the lightest-weight option, but the confirmed two-column-merge defect (shared with plain pdftotext) means it needs pdfplumber's layout/column-detection options (not exercised in this quick check) before it could safely feed an automated limitation/future-work extraction step. pymupdf4llm (TOOL-323) avoided this specific defect out of the box in the same test. Evidence: OBS-0601: pip-installed into a scratch venv (369 MB, deleted after the run) and run on the cached CPR PDF (SRC-0123, sha256 73f1223...): extracted all page text in 4.2s, found the References section (unheaded) and the paper's own limitations sentence intact, but its default extract_text() spliced two unrelated columns together at one checked two-column boundary, an error the pdftotext baseline also makes at the same spot; 2026-09-27
- **TOOL-311 Community MCP paper-search servers (Crossref/OpenAlex/Semantic Scholar/arXiv/DBLP wrappers)** (Assess): Multiple community MCP servers exist that wrap Crossref/OpenAlex/Semantic Scholar/arXiv/DBLP search, none official or particularly authoritative; the already-connected PubMed MCP is the only first-party one available here and it is biomedical-only. None of the surveyed community servers offer a discovery capability this agent doesn't already have directly through polite_get.py against the same free APIs, so adding one would mean extra install/maintenance surface for no coverage gain. Revisit only if a future agent needs a scholarly-search MCP wired into a non-Claude-Code client. Evidence: Not installed or run; assessed from Parallel Search results only (query text reconstructed post-compaction, see SRCH-0613)

Capped at Assess by the charter and by the account limit. Evidence: Not tested: requires account for sustained use. Facts from general knowledge, not re-confirmed this session.
- **TOOL-307 Europe PMC REST API** (Assess): Works keyless with a huge index, but its subject-matter centre of gravity (biomedical/life-sciences) barely overlaps PDFPundit's fields (forensics, LangSec, compression, fonts/OCR, IEEE/ACM venues); the same gap the already-connected PubMed MCP has. Keep as a low-priority fallback for the rare life-sciences-adjacent OCR/accessibility paper, not a primary discovery route. Evidence: python3 research/tools/polite_get.py '.../search?query=pdf+repair&format=json' -> HTTP 200, hitCount=879598, 2026-09-27 (probe/europepmc.json)
- **TOOL-309 Lens.org / Dimensions (commercial scholarly search)** (Assess): provenance.method is memory for the account/quota details above (general knowledge of both products, not re-derived from a fresh fetch this session); capped at Assess accordingly, and further capped by the account-signup block. Only worth an account if OpenAlex/Semantic Scholar/CORE prove insufficient in P4 — those three already cover the bulk of our venues keyless or with a free key. - **TOOL-324 Citance/citation-context classification (published methods, e.g. ACL 2022.sdp-1.6) and future-work/limitation sentence extraction** (Assess): Directly answers sub-task 5's 'citation-context tools' question with a real, open-access, peer-reviewed method rather than a hosted product (contrast TOOL-314 scite.ai, which does the same thing behind a paywall). In principle such a classifier could pre-filter candidate limitation/future-work sentences for other agents, but it cannot replace kb_validate.py's exact-quote/page check: at best it narrows which sentences a human or agent then verifies by hand against the real PDF. Worth caching this paper as a proper SRC/CLM record and, if a future agent has GPU/CPU headroom, reproducing or reusing a small citation-context classifier as a P4/P5 pre-filter -- not attempted here to stay inside this session's time budget. Evidence: Found via Parallel Search (SRCH-0617): ACL Anthology 2022.sdp-1.6 reports a fine-tuned RoBERTa classifier for citation-context criticality at 98.84% accuracy; not fetched/cached or run in this session.
- **TOOL-313 Consensus** (Assess): Same charter cap and account block as Elicit. Consensus's yes/no synthesis format is a poor fit for PDFPundit's kind of evidence (verified quotes at a page, not an AI-synthesized answer), so even with an account it would mostly serve as a discovery lead generator, redundant with OpenAlex/Semantic Scholar/CORE. Evidence: Not tested: requires account signup. Facts from general knowledge, not re-confirmed this session.
- **TOOL-312 Elicit** (Assess): Per the charter, hosted AI literature tools are research-only and capped at Assess regardless of capability, and this agent could not create an account to verify anything hands-on. Elicit's extraction-table workflow is conceptually close to what sub-task 5 wants (pre-filtering candidate limitation/future-work quotes), but as a closed hosted product it cannot itself produce kb_validate.py-checkable verified quotes; at best it could suggest candidates for an agent to then verify against the real PDF. Not worth an account yet given GROBID/Nougat + a citation-context classifier (TOOL-324) can approximate the same pre-filtering keylessly. Evidence: Not tested: requires account signup, which is on this agent's never-do list. Facts below come from the Parallel Search results (SRCH-0614); exact figures not independently re-confirmed this session.
- **TOOL-314 scite.ai** (Assess): Conceptually the closest hosted match to sub-task 5 (citation-context classification), but paywalled at the API level and capped at Assess by the charter regardless. TOOL-324 (the open, fine-tunable RoBERTa citance classifier from ACL 2022.sdp-1.6) gives most of the same capability without an account, license fee, or vendor lock-in, and is the preferred route for P4/P5. Evidence: Not tested: requires account signup for API-level access. Facts from general knowledge/Parallel Search leads, not re-confirmed this session.

- **TOOL-325 Dedicated reference manager (e.g. Zotero/BetterBibTeX-style tooling) vs plain JSONL** (Hold): Crossref content negotiation already gives DOI to BibTeX/CSL-JSON on demand, keyless, with no extra service to install or maintain; every source in the KB already carries its DOI in registry.jsonl, so any reference-manager format can be regenerated on demand rather than stored and kept in sync. Introducing a separate reference manager (Zotero, JabRef, etc.) would add a second source of truth to reconcile with the JSONL registries for no capability we lack -- Hold on adopting one. If a human collaborator later wants a browsable/exportable citation library, generate it from registry.jsonl + Crossref content negotiation as a one-off script rather than maintaining a live reference-manager library. Evidence: python3 research/tools/polite_get.py '.../works/10.1109/das.2018.64/transform/application/x-bibtex' -> HTTP 200, valid @inproceedings{...} BibTeX record, 2026-09-27 (probe/das2018.bib); Crossref's content-negotiation also serves CSL-JSON via Accept: application/vnd.citationstyles.csl+json on the same works/<doi> URL
